title: QUIC RFC 9000 Address-Pair Peer Connection-ID Policy Work Item
summary: Add bounded runtime selection and proof for peer-issued connection IDs that are limited to one local/destination address pair and retired when their address pair is no longer active.
planned_changes:
- Track the address pair on which each active peer-issued CID sequence is used.
- Apply peer-CID selection before application-data sends and validated path promotion.
- Preserve bound active-path CIDs when new spare CIDs are advertised.
- Require a spare peer-issued CID before promoting a new address pair.
- Retire CIDs bound to inactive address pairs after successful migration.
- Add focused requirement-home proof for S5P1P2-0006 and S5P1P2-0007.
verification_plan: Run the focused S5P1P2-0006/0007 requirement-home filter, run the full S5P1P2 requirement-home family, run related path-migration regressions, run a Release build, regenerate QUIC coverage triage, validate SpecTrace JSON, and run the full no-build solution test pass when practical.
out_of_scope: Multipath scheduling or multiple active outbound paths.
Preferred-address migration proof beyond existing path transition behavior.
Changing local connection-ID route registration or stateless reset endpoint behavior.
completion_notes: Completed as a bounded peer-CID address-pair policy slice over the existing single-active-path runtime.
